rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.3-2.5 and 3.2 - authors build a SWAT model of the Lower Mekong forced with TRMM/GPM precipitation and GLDAS temperature, calibrate it (2005-2006) and validate it (2001-2004, 2007-2015) against MRC gauge streamflow at six sub-basin outlets. Q2: Section 3.2, Figs. 3-5 - the satellite-forced model explains about 84% of daily streamflow variance in calibration, NSE 0.86-0.95 and ~3.85% monthly error in validation, capturing timing of onset and end of seasonal flow; Section 3.3, Figs. 7-10, Table 5 - the model is used to quantify flood duration (days above MRC flood threshold, e.g. 13 vs 16 days at Mukdahan in 2011), 7-day maximum flow, flow reversals and Colwell predictability of floods/droughts under upstream release scenarios. Q6: Section 2.1, Table 2, Figs. 3-5 - results are reported at basin scale for a 656,518 km2 drainage area and six sub-basins across Thailand, Laos and Cambodia. Q7: Section 3.2 - the model was most sensitive to precipitation correction factors; running without adjustment of the remote-sensing precipitation overestimated streamflow by about 13%, so a separate correction factor per sub-basin was required (Table 3). Q8: Section 4 - authors state model results are uncertain due to errors in input data, parameters and process representation, that monthly aggregation may mask individual event prediction, and Section 3.2 notes the model was slightly off in some peak-flow estimates.
rows.notes: Q2 is accepted because the remote-sensing-driven model is checked against observed gauge streamflow and flood metrics are derived from it; however the study does not explicitly validate flood-event prediction skill (Fig. 10 compares observed flood duration with the +30% scenario, not with a baseline simulation), and peak flows were admittedly slightly off. Q3: only model-vs-gauge validation, one method. Q4: satellite precipitation accuracy itself is not evaluated against ground data; no intermediate variable beyond the simulated streamflow. Q5: six nested stations along one river in one monsoon basin, not distinct regions/climates. Q9: NSE and percent error are validation errors; SD/CV in Table 2 describe observed annual discharge, not the predicted result; SUFI2 was used but no prediction uncertainty bands are reported.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.3-2.5 and 3.2 - own SWAT model runs with satellite forcing calibrated and validated against observed streamflow.
rows.notes: The study reports no result on allocating water resources more efficiently or on water conservation. It quantifies how hypothetical +/-30% upstream release changes alter downstream streamflow variability, predictability and flood duration (Section 3.3, Figs. 7-10, Table 4-5) and states in the Discussion that such results could serve as tools to guide decision makers; this is hydrological information that could feed allocation decisions (a precondition), not evidence of more efficient allocation. Hence upstream = true.

notes: Full text appears complete (abstract through references and appendices). Study is a basin-scale hydrological modelling paper using satellite precipitation (TRMM/GPM) and GLDAS inputs to SWAT for the Lower Mekong; it addresses flood/drought predictability and flood duration under upstream release scenarios, not water allocation or irrigation per se.
